A user will need to review the data available to determine which data should and should not be\ngenerated for export.\n• There are several ways to narrow the data being captured in the files. If choosing to narrow the\npopulation included, please use caution and review all details to ensure you are getting the output\nintended.\n• To access this area of MEDENT, a user must have security clearance for Data\nExport/Import/Connection Table and Electronic Health Information Export.\n• Documents, Triages and Todo's will be created as HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents (UD),\ncontaining a B64-encoded PDF. All documents will be zipped together upon creation and included within\nthe zip file generated for export. All triages will be zipped together upon creation and included within the\nzip file generated for export. All todos will be zipped together upon creation and included within the zip file\ngenerated for export.\n\nImplementation and Utilization\nEach area of the Electronic Health Information Export is defined below. To access this in MEDENT use\nthe following Navigation: Medical Records > Data Export/Import/Connection Table > Electronic Health\nInformation Export.\n\nSetup\n• Create a Setting to indicate any filters needed for patient population, as well as setting to autorun over\nnight, if needed.\nAdd New Setting: Click this to add a new setting for running the export process. When a setting is added,\nit gets a numerical ID assigned to it that will be referenced in other areas.\nID: Each setting gets a numerical ID assigned in chronological order. The significance of this ID is to keep\nmultiple settings distingushed if generating more than one export.\nFilters & Options: Filter the patient population included in the export process. Included are Demographic\nFilters, which Data Feeds are included (at least one is required), Financial Data (Optional), and Additional\nExports of data including Documents, Triages and/or Todos.\nDemographic Criteria\nDoctors: Provider assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nLocations: Location assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nPrimary Care Providers: PCP provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\nReferring Doctors: RDr provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\nAge: Age of patient at the time of the report generation.\nInclude Insurances: Active insurance on the patient account at the time of the report generation,\nregardless of billing order.\nExclude Insurances: Exclude patients with an active insurance on the patient account at the time\nof the report generation, regardless of billing order.\nPatients: Generate the report for only patients selected here. Default is to include All patients.\nPatient Status: Patient status defaults to include only Active patients, but can be adjusted.\nExempt Status: Default is to exclude exempt patients. This option is DM/HM Report Exempt\noption in the Restrictions section of the Patient Status screen.\n\n\fRace: Race assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nEthnicity: Ethnicity assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nSex: Sex assigned to the patient in the patient information (Note: this is not referencing the Sex at\nBirth field, only the Sex field at this time.)\nPrimary/Members: Primary vs Member accounts included based upon selection if practice is\nusing family accounts.\nPortal: Active portal patients or non-portal patients.\nPatient Characteristics: Patient characteristics, as setup in the Patient Status screen.\nData Feeds (Required)\nPatient Files: Defaults to export all data files.\nFinancial Export (Optional)\nExport Financial Data: Select a Data Format Maintenance if you wish to include financial\ninformation in the export. When selected, the system uses the logic in place to generate a History\nTransaction Report with Single Sort for the data points referenced in the Data Format Maintenance. The\nfile format will align with the other text Data Feed files.\nDoctors: Select to include or exclude provider data for the financial piece of this export.\nLocations: Select to include or exclude location data for the financial piece of this export.\nInsurances: Select to include or exclude location data for the financial piece of this export.\nActivity and/or History Files: Select Activity, History or Both to be included\nAdditional Exports (Optional)\nExport Documents: Include or exclude documents based on document code and/or chart button.\nExport Traiges: Include or exclude triages based on reason code.\nInclude Blank: Check this box to include triages without a reason code indicated.\nExport ToDos: Include or exclude todos based on reason code.\nInclude Blank: Check this box to include todos without a reason code indicated.\nPrivacy Alert: Check this box to exclude patients with a privacy alert on their account. Default is\nunchecked, which includes these patients.\nBy E-Superbill: Check this box to generate the patient listed based upon E-Superbill rather than the\ndefault of basing the population on booked appointments.\nAutorun: Check this box to schedule the report to Autorun during the nightly processes.\nTime Frame/Date Range: The frame indicated tells the system the population of patients with an\nAppointment or E-Superbill in their chart to include in the export.\nScheduled: This is the date the report will kick off to generate the data.\nDelete: Select this to remove the setting. Once deleted, you cannot re-access this setting. A brand new\nsetting will need to be created.\nAt the top of the Setup page includes a Log of any changes made to this area as well as a place to\nindicate additional custom-created Closed Superbill status's that should be captured, if the setting is being\nexported by Superbill's instead of Appointments.\n\nCreate\nEach setting created in the Setup area is also listed in Create. Review options and further limit selection,\nif needed to manually generate data for export.\nID: Each setting gets a numerical ID assigned in chronological order. The significance of this ID is to keep\nmultiple settings distingushed if generating more than one export.\nFilters & Options: Filters are adjusted in the Setup area. This screen only shows a reference point to\nalert the user that these filters are applied to anything generated from this screen as well.\nData Feed: Include all or limit the data being generated further beyond what's already limited in the Setup\narea.\n\n\fPatient(s): Include all or select specific patient(s) to generate for export.\nPrivacy Alert: References the Setup area for this setting and displays if patients with a privacy alert are\nexcluded. View only.\nSelected By: Referenced the Setup area for this setting and displays if patients are queried based on\nAppointments or E-Superbills. View only.\nFrom: Indicate the start date for which the patient population should be queried.\nTo: Indicate an end date for which the patient population should be queried.\nCreate: After all options have been reviewed, select this button to begin generating the data for export.\n\nSend\nCompleted reports that have not exported out of the MEDENT system will remain in the Send screen until\nsent to an external destination using \"Send\" or deleted.\nFiles with an asterisk indicate they have been generated with the intention of saving the data to the Local\nPC. These files will remain in the Send screen until deleted. They can be exported at any time.\nFile Name: Complete path and file name that has been generated for export.\nFile Date: Date and time the file was created.\nSend: Exports file(s) to their intended destination, as defined in the Control File. The File Name\nreferenced the setting# and Connection Name for which the export is intended to be sent.\nView: Click on a file or check the box and select View to open contents of file.\nDelete: Delete all selected files. Once removed from this list, the files cannot be restored.\nExport to PC: Save selected file to your Local PC at the destination of your choice. Use caution when\nexporting, saving and sending PHI to ensure HIPAA guidelines are followed.\n\nControl File\nSetting #: Setting ID which aligns with the Setup and Create areas.\nFilename: Enter the prefix the filename should include. Special characters are not allowed, including\nspaces.\nFile Format: Indicate the delimiter desired from the options available.\nPIPE (Quotes)\nPIPE (without Quotes)\nCSV (Quotes)\nCSV (without Quotes)\nName Format: Select the desired filename suffix used for filename creation. From date and through date\nare the dates for which the patient population has been based upon. Process ID is the unique ID for the\nsession that generated the file.\n_<File create date and timestamp>_<Practice ID>_<Process ID>\n_<File create date and timestamp>_<Process ID>\n_<From date>_<Through date>_<Process ID>\n_<From date>_<Through date_<Practice ID>_<Process ID>\nZip Files: Check this box to zip all files together for export.\nConnection: Select a connection from the Connection Table to export the data to a designated\ndestination, or select For export to Local PC to generate the file on the server so that it can then be\nexported upon completion.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"85db5316-4fcc-40b4-a3b3-26f9c343c9e8","uuid":"f41daec8-9589-4e14-84b3-3ebb5c3f7eaa","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"Electronic Health Information Export\n• Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export contains “ electronic protected health information” (ePHI) as\ndefined in 45 CFR 164.501, along with additional data in the patient chart.\n• Psychotherapy notes or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil,\ncriminal, or administrative action or proceeding are not automatically included, nor excluded from the\nexport. A user will need to review the data available to determine which data should and should not be\ngenerated for export.\n• There are several ways to narrow the data being captured in the files. If choosing to narrow the\npopulation included, please use caution and review all details to ensure you are getting the output\nintended.\n• To access this area of MEDENT, a user must have security clearance for Data\nExport/Import/Connection Table and Electronic Health Information Export.\n• Documents, Triages and Todo's will be created as HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents (UD),\ncontaining a B64-encoded PDF. All documents will be zipped together upon creation and included within\nthe zip file generated for export. All triages will be zipped together upon creation and included within the\nzip file generated for export. All todos will be zipped together upon creation and included within the zip file\ngenerated for export.\n\nImplementation and Utilization\nEach area of the Electronic Health Information Export is defined below. To access this in MEDENT use\nthe following Navigation: Medical Records > Data Export/Import/Connection Table > Electronic Health\nInformation Export.\n\nSetup\n• Create a Setting to indicate any filters needed for patient population, as well as setting to autorun over\nnight, if needed.\nAdd New Setting: Click this to add a new setting for running the export process. When a setting is added,\nit gets a numerical ID assigned to it that will be referenced in other areas.\nID: Each setting gets a numerical ID assigned in chronological order. The significance of this ID is to keep\nmultiple settings distingushed if generating more than one export.\nFilters & Options: Filter the patient population included in the export process. Included are Demographic\nFilters, which Data Feeds are included (at least one is required), Financial Data (Optional), and Additional\nExports of data including Documents, Triages and/or Todos.\nDemographic Criteria\nDoctors: Provider assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nLocations: Location assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nPrimary Care Providers: PCP provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\nReferring Doctors: RDr provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\nAge: Age of patient at the time of the report generation.\nInclude Insurances: Active insurance on the patient account at the time of the report generation,\nregardless of billing order.\nExclude Insurances: Exclude patients with an active insurance on the patient account at the time\nof the report generation, regardless of billing order.\nPatients: Generate the report for only patients selected here. Default is to include All patients.\nPatient Status: Patient status defaults to include only Active patients, but can be adjusted.\nExempt Status: Default is to exclude exempt patients. This option is DM/HM Report Exempt\noption in the Restrictions section of the Patient Status screen.\n\n\fRace: Race assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nEthnicity: Ethnicity assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nSex: Sex assigned to the patient in the patient information (Note: this is not referencing the Sex at\nBirth field, only the Sex field at this time.)\nPrimary/Members: Primary vs Member accounts included based upon selection if practice is\nusing family accounts.\nPortal: Active portal patients or non-portal patients.\nPatient Characteristics: Patient characteristics, as setup in the Patient Status screen.\nData Feeds (Required)\nPatient Files: Defaults to export all data files.\nFinancial Export (Optional)\nExport Financial Data: Select a Data Format Maintenance if you wish to include financial\n\n\n\n=== Encounter_File_Specification.pdf ===\nEncounter File Specification\nField Information (EHI) Export contains “ electronic protected health information” (ePHI) as\n   296→defined in 45 CFR 164.501, along with additional data in the patient chart.\n   297→• Psychotherapy notes or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil,\n   298→criminal, or administrative action or proceeding are not automatically included, nor excluded from the\n   299→export. A user will need to review the data available to determine which data should and should not be\n   300→generated for export.\n   301→• There are several ways to narrow the data being captured in the files. If choosing to narrow the\n   302→population included, please use caution and review all details to ensure you are getting the output\n   303→intended.\n   304→• To access this area of MEDENT, a user must have security clearance for Data\n   305→Export/Import/Connection Table and Electronic Health Information Export.\n   306→• Documents, Triages and Todo's will be created as HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents (UD),\n   307→containing a B64-encoded PDF. All documents will be zipped together upon creation and included within\n   308→the zip file generated for export. All triages will be zipped together upon creation and included within the\n   309→zip file generated for export. All todos will be zipped together upon creation and included within the zip file\n   310→generated for export.\n   311→\n   312→Implementation and Utilization\n   313→Each area of the Electronic Health Information Export is defined below. To access this in MEDENT use\n   314→the following Navigation: Medical Records > Data Export/Import/Connection Table > Electronic Health\n   315→Information Export.\n   316→\n   317→Setup\n   318→• Create a Setting to indicate any filters needed for patient population, as well as setting to autorun over\n   319→night, if needed.\n   320→Add New Setting: Click this to add a new setting for running the export process. When a setting is added,\n   321→it gets a numerical ID assigned to it that will be referenced in other areas.\n   322→ID: Each setting gets a numerical ID assigned in chronological order. The significance of this ID is to keep\n   323→multiple settings distingushed if generating more than one export.\n   324→Filters & Options: Filter the patient population included in the export process. Included are Demographic\n   325→Filters, which Data Feeds are included (at least one is required), Financial Data (Optional), and Additional\n   326→Exports of data including Documents, Triages and/or Todos.\n   327→Demographic Criteria\n   328→Doctors: Provider assigned to the patient in the patient information.\n   329→Locations: Location assigned to the patient in the patient information.\n   330→Primary Care Providers: PCP provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\n   331→Referring Doctors: RDr provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\n   332→Age: Age of patient at the time of the report generation.\n   333→Include Insurances: Active insurance on the patient account at the time of the report generation,\n   334→regardless of billing order.\n   335→Exclude Insurances: Exclude patients with an active insurance on the patient account at the time\n   336→of the report generation, regardless of billing order.\n   337→Patients: Generate the report for only patients selected here. Default is to include All patients.\n   338→Patient Status: Patient status defaults to include only Active patients, but can be adjusted.\n   339→Exempt Status: Default is to exclude exempt patients. This option is DM/HM Report Exempt\n   340→option in the Restrictions section of the Patient Status screen.\n   341→\n   342→\fRace: Race assigned to the patient in the patient information.\n   343→Ethnicity: Ethnicity assigned to the patient in the patient information.\n   344→Sex: Sex assigned to the patient in the patient information (Note: this is not referencing the Sex at\n   345→Birth field, only the Sex field at this time.)\n   346→Primary/Members: Primary vs Member accounts included based upon selection if practice is\n   347→using family accounts.\n   348→Portal: Active portal patients or non-portal patients.\n   349→Patient Characteristics: Patient characteristics, as setup in the Patient Status screen.\n   350→Data Feeds (Required)\n   351→Patient Files: Defaults to export all data files.\n   352→Financial Export (Optional)\n   353→Export Financial Data: Select a Data Format Maintenance if you wish to include financial\n   354→\n   355→\n   356→\n   357→=== A user will need to review the data available to determine which data should and should not be\ngenerated for export.\n• There are several ways to narrow the data being captured in the files. If choosing to narrow the\npopulation included, please use caution and review all details to ensure you are getting the output\nintended.\n• To access this area of MEDENT, a user must have security clearance for Data\nExport/Import/Connection Table and Electronic Health Information Export.\n• Documents, Triages and Todo's will be created as HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents (UD),\ncontaining a B64-encoded PDF. All documents will be zipped together upon creation and included within\nthe zip file generated for export. All triages will be zipped together upon creation and included within the\nzip file generated for export. All todos will be zipped together upon creation and included within the zip file\ngenerated for export.\n\nImplementation and Utilization\nEach area of the Electronic Health Information Export is defined below. To access this in MEDENT use\nthe following Navigation: Medical Records > Data Export/Import/Connection Table > Electronic Health\nInformation Export.\n\nSetup\n• Create a Setting to indicate any filters needed for patient population, as well as setting to autorun over\nnight, if needed.\nAdd New Setting: Click this to add a new setting for running the export process. When a setting is added,\nit gets a numerical ID assigned to it that will be referenced in other areas.\nID: Each setting gets a numerical ID assigned in chronological order. The significance of this ID is to keep\nmultiple settings distingushed if generating more than one export.\nFilters & Options: Filter the patient population included in the export process. Included are Demographic\nFilters, which Data Feeds are included (at least one is required), Financial Data (Optional), and Additional\nExports of data including Documents, Triages and/or Todos.\nDemographic Criteria\nDoctors: Provider assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nLocations: Location assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nPrimary Care Providers: PCP provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\nReferring Doctors: RDr provider assigned to the patients in the patient information.\nAge: Age of patient at the time of the report generation.\nInclude Insurances: Active insurance on the patient account at the time of the report generation,\nregardless of billing order.\nExclude Insurances: Exclude patients with an active insurance on the patient account at the time\nof the report generation, regardless of billing order.\nPatients: Generate the report for only patients selected here. Default is to include All patients.\nPatient Status: Patient status defaults to include only Active patients, but can be adjusted.\nExempt Status: Default is to exclude exempt patients. This option is DM/HM Report Exempt\noption in the Restrictions section of the Patient Status screen.\n\n\fRace: Race assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nEthnicity: Ethnicity assigned to the patient in the patient information.\nSex: Sex assigned to the patient in the patient information (Note: this is not referencing the Sex at\nBirth field, only the Sex field at this time.)\nPrimary/Members: Primary vs Member accounts included based upon selection if practice is\nusing family accounts.\nPortal: Active portal patients or non-portal patients.\nPatient Characteristics: Patient characteristics, as setup in the Patient Status screen.\nData Feeds (Required)\nPatient Files: Defaults to export all data files.\nFinancial Export (Optional)\nExport Financial Data: Select a Data Format Maintenance if you wish to include financial\n\n\n\n=== Encounter_File_Specification.pdf ===\nEncounter File Specification\nField This is one of the better (b)(10) implementations encountered: it is not a repurposed FHIR endpoint but a dedicated export module with its own documentation, field-level specifications, and configurable export settings.\n\n### Export Architecture\n\nThe EHI export is accessed via: **Medical Records > Data Export/Import/Connection Table > Electronic Health Information Export**. It has four operational areas:\n\n1. **Setup** — Configure export settings: patient population filters (by provider, location, age, insurance, race, ethnicity, sex, status), data feeds to include, optional financial data, and optional document/triage/todo exports. Supports autorun scheduling for overnight batch processing.\n\n2. **Create** — Review settings and trigger data generation for a specific date range. Can be further narrowed to specific patients.\n\n3. **Send** — Completed exports are queued for transmission to external destinations or download to local PC.\n\n4. **Control File** — Configures output format:\n   - **Delimiters**: PIPE (with/without quotes), CSV (with/without quotes)\n   - **Filename format**: Configurable with create date, practice ID, process ID, date ranges\n   - **ZIP compression**: Optional\n   - **Connection**: Can route to configured destinations or local PC download\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe export produces **delimited text files** (CSV or pipe-delimited). Each data domain has its own file with a documented field specification. Documents, triages, and todos are exported as **HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents** containing Base64-encoded PDFs, zipped together.\n\n### Documentation Corpus\n\n33 PDF file specifications severity, criticality)\n- Diagnoses (encounter-level and problem list)\n- Medications (prescriptions with full SIG, NDC, RxNorm, administration records)\n- Immunizations (with CVX, lot numbers, records (data disclosure tracking)\n\n**Domains potentially missing or unclear:**\n- **Triages (messages)**: The setup document mentions including triages and todos in the export as C-CDA documents, but there is no dedicated field specification for these. They appear to be exported as unstructured PDFs rather than structured data.\n- **Patient portal messages**: No explicit specification for portal message content (though they may be captured under documents/triages).\n- **Telehealth encounter data**: No dedicated telehealth-specific fields beyond standard encounter data, though the appointment spec does include an \"E-Visit\" status.\n- **Clinical note content**: Progress notes and documents export metadata and the document itself as a C-CDA-wrapped PDF. The actual text/structured content of notes is not broken into discrete fields — but this is reasonable since clinical notes are inherently unstructured.\n- **Scanned images**: The document listing includes document metadata but the actual image/scan content export is handled through the C-CDA document wrapping mechanism.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **delimited text files** (CSV or pipe-delimited) for structured data and **HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents** for documents, triages, and todos. This is a pragmatic, well-designed approach:\n\n- The delimited text format is universally readable and doesn't force clinical data into a standard that may not fit well\n- Coded fields use standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, NDC, CPT, ICD-10)\n- UUIDs provide stable record identifiers\n- Documents are wrapped in C-CDA for interoperability while preserving the original content as PDF\n\nRelationships between entities are expressed through shared identifiers:\n- `patient_mrn` and `MEDENT_id` link records to patients\n- `encounter_id` (E-Superbill number) links records to encounters\n- `provider_id` links to the Provider file\n- `location_id` links to the Location file\n- `plan_id` links patient insurance to the InsurancePlan file\n\nThis is **not** a FHIR-based export (the FHIR API is documented separately for g(10) compliance). The EHI export is a purpose-built, configurable data extraction system that exports directly from MEDENT's internal data structures.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Excellent.** This is among the best-documented EHI exports:\n\n- Every data file has its own PDF specification with field names, descriptions, and example output\n- Field names are consistent (snake_case), matching actual export column headers\n- Descriptions reference specific MEDENT UI screens and data sources, making the mapping traceable\n- Standard code systems are explicitly called out (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, etc.)\n- The main Setup document provides clear workflow instructions with navigation paths\n- The financial export leverages a pre-existing, comprehensive 750-field configuration system\n- The Info File provides export metadata including criteria used and record counts per file\n\nAreas for improvement:\n- Data types are not formally specified (no explicit \"string\", \"date\", \"integer\" declarations), though example output makes types inferrable\n- Value sets for coded fields are not enumerated in the specifications (e.g., what are the valid `status` values for appointments?) — though some are documented inline (e.g., verification_status: \"Confirmed, Unconfirmed, Refuted\")\n- No formal schema file (XSD, JSON Schema, etc.) — field specs are only in PDF\n- Cardinality is not formally specified (which fields are required vs optional)\n- The financial export documentation requires navigating to the separate ASCII Field List HTML manual page\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n**Granularity**: Field-level documentation with names, descriptions, and examples for all 33 data files. The Patient file alone has ~80 fields. Total structured fields across all EHI specs: ~648, plus 750 configurable financial fields.\n\n**Coded fields**: Standard terminologies are documented (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, NDC, CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10, UNII). However, proprietary value sets (appointment types, document codes, etc.) are not enumerated.\n\n**Relationships**: Cross-file relationships are implied through shared field names (patient_mrn, MEDENT_id, encounter_id, provider_id, location_id, plan_id) rather than formally documented with a relationship diagram.\n\n**Specialty coverage**: Notably includes ophthalmology/optometry data (Eye/Contact Script with keratometry, sphere, cylinder, axis, etc.) and OB/GYN data (antepartum records, delivery outcomes, birth weights). This demonstrates real (b)(10) thinking — exporting specialty clinical data that would never appear in a standard FHIR US Core export.\n\n**Versioning**: No explicit version number or change history on the specifications. The main Setup PDF title includes \"Part1Img3912SUPPROGC\" in its metadata, suggesting it was created from the MEDENT documentation system. PDF creation date is November 30, 2023, roughly contemporaneous with the September 2023 certification.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.medent.com/onc/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (PDFs downloadable via curl; ASCII Field List page needed browser for JS rendering but content is also in HTML source)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (EHI section clearly labeled on the ONC page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (standard User-Agent header sufficient)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n- **Spaces in PDF URLs**: The PDF filenames contain spaces (e.g., \"Allergy File Specification.pdf\"), requiring URL-encoding (`%20`) for successful download via curl. records (data disclosure tracking)\n\n**Domains potentially missing or unclear:**\n- **Triages (messages)**: The setup document mentions including triages and todos in the export as C-CDA documents, but there is no dedicated field specification for these. They appear to be exported as unstructured PDFs rather than structured data.\n- **Patient portal messages**: No explicit specification for portal message content (though they may be captured under documents/triages).\n- **Telehealth encounter data**: No dedicated telehealth-specific fields beyond standard encounter data, though the appointment spec does include an \"E-Visit\" status.\n- **Clinical note content**: Progress notes and documents export metadata and the document itself as a C-CDA-wrapped PDF. The actual text/structured content of notes is not broken into discrete fields — but this is reasonable since clinical notes are inherently unstructured.\n- **Scanned images**: The document listing includes document metadata but the actual image/scan content export is handled through the C-CDA document wrapping mechanism.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **delimited text files** (CSV or pipe-delimited) for structured data and **HL7 C-CDA 2.1 Unstructured Documents** for documents, triages, and todos. This is a pragmatic, well-designed approach:\n\n- The delimited text format is universally readable and doesn't force clinical data into a standard that may not fit well\n- Coded fields use standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, NDC, CPT, ICD-10)\n- UUIDs provide stable record identifiers\n- Documents are wrapped in C-CDA for interoperability while preserving the original content as PDF\n\nRelationships between entities are expressed through shared identifiers:\n- `patient_mrn` and `MEDENT_id` link records to patients\n- `encounter_id` (E-Superbill number) links records to encounters\n- `provider_id` links to the Provider file\n- `location_id` links to the Location file\n- `plan_id` links patient insurance to the InsurancePlan file\n\nThis is **not** a FHIR-based export (the FHIR API is documented separately for g(10) compliance). The EHI export is a purpose-built, configurable data extraction system that exports directly from MEDENT's internal data structures.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Excellent.** This is among the best-documented EHI exports:\n\n- Every data file has its own PDF specification with field names, descriptions, and example output\n- Field names are consistent (snake_case), matching actual export column headers\n- Descriptions reference specific MEDENT UI screens and data sources, making the mapping traceable\n- Standard code systems are explicitly called out (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, etc.)\n- The main Setup document provides clear workflow instructions with navigation paths\n- The financial export leverages a pre-existing, comprehensive 750-field configuration system\n- The Info File provides export metadata including criteria used and record counts per file\n\nAreas for improvement:\n- Data types are not formally specified (no explicit \"string\", \"date\", \"integer\" declarations), though example output makes types inferrable\n- Value sets for coded fields are not enumerated in the specifications (e.g., what are the valid `status` values for appointments?) — though some are documented inline (e.g., verification_status: \"Confirmed, Unconfirmed, Refuted\")\n- No formal schema file (XSD, JSON Schema, etc.) — field specs are only in PDF\n- Cardinality is not formally specified (which fields are required vs optional)\n- The financial export documentation requires navigating to the separate ASCII Field List HTML manual page\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n**Granularity**: Field-level documentation with names, descriptions, and examples for all 33 data files. The Patient file alone has ~80 fields. Total structured fields across all EHI specs: ~648, plus 750 configurable financial fields.\n\n**Coded fields**: Standard terminologies are documented (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, NDC, CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10, UNII). However, proprietary value sets (appointment types, document codes, etc.) are not enumerated.\n\n**Relationships**: Cross-file relationships are implied through shared field names (patient_mrn, MEDENT_id, encounter_id, provider_id, location_id, plan_id) rather than formally documented with a relationship diagram.\n\n**Specialty coverage**: Notably includes ophthalmology/optometry data (Eye/Contact Script with keratometry, sphere, cylinder, axis, etc.) and OB/GYN data (antepartum records, delivery outcomes, birth weights). This demonstrates real (b)(10) thinking — exporting specialty clinical data that would never appear in a standard FHIR US Core export.\n\n**Versioning**: No explicit version number or change history on the specifications. The main Setup PDF title includes \"Part1Img3912SUPPROGC\" in its metadata, suggesting it was created from the MEDENT documentation system. PDF creation date is November 30, 2023, roughly contemporaneous with the September 2023 certification.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.medent.com/onc/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (PDFs downloadable via curl; ASCII Field List page needed browser for JS rendering but content is also in HTML source)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (EHI section clearly labeled on the ONC page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none (standard User-Agent header sufficient)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n- **Spaces in PDF URLs**: The PDF filenames contain spaces (e.g., \"Allergy File Specification.pdf\"), requiring URL-encoding (`%20`) for successful download via curl. This is the only spec that delegates its content to an external reference.\n\nNo dead ends, no login walls, no Cloudflare blocks.
